title: The Meeting Outside Working Hours
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の制度・医療助言・調査・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A public organization may invite residents to express their opinions before making a decision that affects a shared space.
sentences.ja: 公共組織は共有空間に影響する判断を下す前に住民へ意見表明を促すことがある。

sentences.en: The number of people who participate can provide useful information about the response to such an invitation.
sentences.ja: 参加者数は招待への反応について有用な情報を提供し得る。

sentences.en: However, participation also depends on whether the arrangement makes it practically possible for different groups of residents to contribute.
sentences.ja: しかし参加はその仕組みによって異なる住民集団が実際に意見を出せるかにも依存する。

sentences.en: The opinions expressed at a meeting are not necessarily representative of everyone who has an interest in the decision.
sentences.ja: 説明会で表明された意見は判断に関心がある全員を必ずしも代表しない。

sentences.en: Imagine a town considering changes to the opening hours of a community facility.
sentences.ja: 地域施設の開館時間変更を検討する町を想像しよう。

sentences.en: The officials organize a meeting during the afternoon, when staff members are normally available to answer questions.
sentences.ja: 職員は通常質問回答ができる午後に説明会を開く。

sentences.en: Several visitors support the proposal, while relatively few objections are expressed during the discussion.
sentences.ja: 数名が提案を支持し、議論では比較的少数の反対しか表明されない。

sentences.en: An official suggests that the absence of strong disagreement demonstrates that the proposal is widely accepted throughout the community.
sentences.ja: ある職員は強い反対がないことが地域全体に広く受け入れられていると示すと主張する。

sentences.en: Another official asks whether people working during the afternoon have had a realistic opportunity to attend the meeting.
sentences.ja: 別の職員は午後働く人々に現実的な出席機会があったか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The proposed changes might be particularly significant to those who use the facility after finishing their daily responsibilities.
sentences.ja: 提案された変更は日々の責任を終えた後施設を使う人にとり特に重要かもしれない。

sentences.en: The officials recognize that the circumstances preventing some residents from attending may also influence their opinions about the proposal.
sentences.ja: 一部住民の出席を妨げる事情は提案への意見にも影響し得ると認識する。

sentences.en: Consequently, they distinguish a lack of expressed objections from evidence of widespread agreement.
sentences.ja: そこで表明された反対がないことと広範な同意の証拠を区別する。

sentences.en: The organization considers collecting written responses and offering an additional opportunity for conversation at a different time.
sentences.ja: 組織は書面回答を集め別時間に追加会話機会を提供することを検討する。

sentences.en: These methods might reach additional residents, although each would have its own practical limitations.
sentences.ja: 方法は追加住民に届き得るがそれぞれ実務上の限界を持つだろう。

sentences.en: The fictional case does not establish which consultation procedures are legally required or which methods produce representative results in actual communities.
sentences.ja: 架空例はどの相談手続が法的に必要か、どの方法が実際に代表性ある結果を生むか確定しない。

sentences.en: It instead highlights a question about the connection between access to a discussion and the conclusions drawn from it.
sentences.ja: 代わりに議論へのアクセスとそこから導く結論の関係という問いを強調する。

sentences.en: Inviting people to participate is an important step, but it cannot by itself guarantee that the resulting discussion includes every relevant perspective.
sentences.ja: 参加を促すのは重要な一歩だが、それだけでは議論に関連する全視点が含まれることを保証できない。

sentences.en: An organization interpreting the responses it receives should consider how the conditions of participation may have shaped those responses.
sentences.ja: 受け取った回答を解釈する組織は参加条件が回答をどう形作ったか考えるべきだ。

sentences.en: Public silence can have more than one explanation, and an accurate assessment requires attention to those possibilities.
sentences.ja: 公の沈黙には複数の説明があり、正確な評価にはその可能性への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: The time of a meeting may therefore matter as much as the questions discussed during it.
sentences.ja: したがって説明会の時間は議論される問いと同じほど重要になり得る。

vocabulary.definition: in a way possible in practice
things one is expected to do
act of seeking advice or views

questions.prompt: Why may participation numbers be insufficient on their own?
options: They depend partly on people's opportunities to take part.
Every resident always attends public meetings.
The opinions expressed are necessarily false.
questions.explanation_ja: 参加機会が数に影響する。

questions.prompt: What may an organization invite residents to do?
When is the imaginary meeting held?
What assumption does one official make?
options: Few expressed objections imply widespread agreement.
The proposal has no impact on opening hours.
Attendance has already been measured accurately.
questions.explanation_ja: 反対の少なさを同意とみなす。

options: Residents who have moved away permanently.

questions.prompt: Why might absence be related to opinions?
options: All absent residents have identical views.
Work schedules may affect both attendance and the need for opening hours.
People who work never use public facilities.
questions.explanation_ja: 勤務日程が参加条件と必要の両方に影響する。

options: Written responses and another meeting time.
A decision based only on attendance.

questions.prompt: Why are the methods presented as possibilities rather than rules?
options: They are proven to represent every resident.
The fictional case establishes universal law.
Their actual usefulness and legal requirements depend on real conditions.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の効果・法的要件は未確定。

options: A way of viewing a matter.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the argument?
options: Public consultation should account for how participation conditions shape the opinions collected.
Few objections always establish community-wide support.
Every meeting must take place in the afternoon.
The only useful measure is attendance.
questions.explanation_ja: 参加条件が回答を形作る。

grammar.focus: who has an interest in the decision
when staff members are normally available
grammar.explanation_ja: 関係副詞whenが午後の時間を説明。

paraphrases.source: The opinions expressed at a meeting are not necessarily representative of everyone who has an interest in the decision.
paraphrases.rewrite: The participants' opinions may not represent all interested residents.

paraphrases.source: The officials organize a meeting during the afternoon, when staff members are normally available to answer questions.
paraphrases.rewrite: Officials select an afternoon because staff can answer questions then.

paraphrases.source: The officials recognize that the circumstances preventing some residents from attending may also influence their opinions about the proposal.
paraphrases.rewrite: The factors limiting attendance can affect residents' views as well.

paraphrases.source: Inviting people to participate is an important step, but it cannot by itself guarantee that the resulting discussion includes every relevant perspective.
paraphrases.rewrite: An invitation alone does not ensure that all relevant perspectives are included.

discourse.role_ja: 法的手順でなく概念を説明。
